metadata.principle: Energy sovereignty means retaining sufficient controllable generation, storage, flexible demand and infrastructure to withstand climate, hydrological and market shocks while using interstate trade strategically. It does not mean autarky or zero imports.

energyproject_context.note: Energy Project public chart inputs; India-wide, not Kerala telemetry.

official_observed_2024_25.note: Kerala Economic Review 2025 / KSEBL annual FY2024-25 reference values.

baseline_summary.note: Derived only after historical calibration checks.

weather.note: NASA POWER representative-point hourly weather; not station or plant telemetry.

era5_reanalysis.note: Copernicus ERA5 hourly acquisition: 5 / 10 expected files; manifest only on the website.

grid_india_psp.note: Current API integration is configured; processed FY2024-25 rows not in this bundle yet.

kseb_project_inventory.note: 70 distinct project records parsed; portal lists 87 entries. Portal statuses and dates are retained as reported.

kseb_historical_export.note: 10 normalized historical series from the user-supplied KSEB export bundle. This adds annual capacity, generation, system-balance, network, consumer and loss history; it does not contain an hourly load chronology.

hourly_load_proxy.note: 8760-hour reconstruction constrained by SLDC daily energy and CEA aggregate hourly references; this is not measured telemetry.

hourly_state_load.note: No authenticated FY2024-25 Kerala 8760/35040 state-load chronology is published in this bundle.

scope.initial_model: A single aggregate electrical bus represents the whole Kerala system, not Kochi or any other city.
scope.next_model: A reduced zonal network across Kerala, once transmission and regional demand data are validated.
scope.atlas_status: Illustrative research locations only; not a complete transmission or district asset inventory.
scope.coverage_rule: Statewide scope does not imply that district demand, all grid assets, or GIS constraints are already measured or connected.

observed.purpose: Official observed Kerala power-system values used to validate the reconstructed SLDC/Grid-India historical baseline. These are not model outputs and are not combined with planning-scenario values unless their scopes match.

circular_industry.principle: A by-product or recovery claim enters the Kerala 2040 model only when its process origin, quantity/capacity or composition, recovery route, and source are explicit enough to support a mass/value balance. Planned projects are kept separate from commissioned facilities.

scenarios.name: Business As Usual
scenarios.description: Existing structural import dependence, hydro exposure and moderate local RE growth.

scenarios.name: Maximum Local Generation
scenarios.description: Stress-test aggressive local generation build-out before ecological constraints are tightened. Intended to expose land, biodiversity, water and system-cost consequences rather than to be presented as a recommendation.

scenarios.name: Solar Storage
scenarios.description: Rooftop, floating and suitable ground PV with BESS/pumped storage and hydro balancing.

scenarios.name: Integrated Sovereignty
scenarios.description: Diversified generation, strategic reservoir dispatch, distributed storage, demand response, EV smart charging/V2G, cooling flexibility and strong interconnection.

scenarios.name: Ecological Sovereignty
scenarios.description: S3 with strict biodiversity, forest, watershed, wetland, slope, landslide, coastal and land-use constraints fed back as technology-specific capacity limits.

dry_hydro.description: Multi-season adverse inflow/hydrology case derived from climate/hydrology data.

cloudy_low_solar.description: Sustained low-solar period preserving observed weather covariance.

ev_surge.description: Higher-than-central electrification trajectory with unmanaged and managed charging variants.

import_restriction.description: Temporary reduction in interstate transfer availability, not permanent isolation.

extreme_monsoon_flood.description: Infrastructure and hydrology stress with ecological/resilience implications.

cstep_2024.title: Kerala Energy Transition Roadmap 2040
cstep_2024.publisher: Center for Study of Science, Technology and Policy (CSTEP)
cstep_2024.methodology_note: Demand forecast is based on historical category consumption and adds explicit EV and induction-cooking demand. Its FY22 load shape was derived from FY16 15-minute data and extrapolated, so it is a useful published benchmark rather than a substitute for a current measured hourly series.
cstep_2024.caveat: CSTEP capacity additions and demand trajectories represent one published study's scenario architecture. Kerala2040 will reproduce or challenge them using newer measured data, climate stress and explicit ecological constraints.

kerala_cn50_2026.title: Carbon Neutral Kerala by 2050
kerala_cn50_2026.publisher: Directorate of Environment and Climate Change, Government of Kerala / Vasudha Foundation
kerala_cn50_2026.note: This newer pathway explicitly treats interstate procurement as a flexible option, excludes exceptionally wet 2021-22 hydro PLF from its baseline, and reports in-state renewable resource potential as insufficient for projected demand beyond 2030.
kerala_cn50_2026.caveat: The 2026 CN50 and 2024 CSTEP studies use different scopes, assumptions and electrification trajectories. Their 2040 demand values must not be blended into a single target.

energyproject.note: Secondary national data attributed by the publisher to NLDC, IEX and CEA. Latest-month profiles are averaged from public quarter-hour chart inputs. Not Kerala telemetry, not a Kerala delivered tariff, and not a replacement for SLDC data. Source dates and partial-month coverage are retained.

kerala_sldc.note: System-statistics and storage reports expose independent historical date forms. Their accounting labels are preserved rather than collapsed into one import metric.

grid_india_daily_psp.note: MOP_E provides official per-state daily peak-demand and energy metrics. TimeSeries in these workbooks is national, not a Kerala hourly series.

kerala_spb.note: Economic Review 2025 provides the current official FY2024-25 Kerala baseline, including capacity, annual sales, imports/exports, peak demand and EV registrations.

kseb_pms.note: The project-management portal is reachable even when the main kseb.in site is not. Its tracker landing page carries an older data-as-of label, so project dates are treated as project records rather than a guaranteed current operational snapshot.

kseb_historical_export.note: Official KSEB table/chart exports supplied by the project author on 2026-09-18. Values are stored as exported and used as historical evidence; the bundle does not contain Kerala's raw hourly or 15-minute state-load chronology.

cea.note: CEA publications are used for national/state cross-checks and planning benchmarks, not to replace more granular Kerala SLDC observations. The official Daily Power Supply Position route is retained as a fallback cross-check when Grid-India's file API is unavailable from automated runners.

kserc.note: Regulatory orders are the preferred source for approved cost and tariff assumptions.

era5.note: ERA5 is the main reanalysis source. Kerala 2040 stores derived model inputs and provenance rather than committing the full raw reanalysis archive.

nasa_power.note: Representative point data are weather inputs, not a claim that one point represents statewide resource potential. Spatial weighting comes later.

data_gov_in.note: One account-level API key applies across API-enabled OGD resources. The API host has timed out from GitHub-hosted runners, so downloadable resources and primary-source alternatives are retained as fallbacks.

niti_iced.organisation: NITI Aayog India Climate and Energy Dashboard
niti_iced.note: No stable documented public API is assumed. ICED is used to discover and cross-check datasets; primary official sources remain preferred.

india_wris.note: Used to extend hydro chronology beyond the Kerala SLDC storage reports when accessible.

niwe.note: NIWE publishes the 150 m wind atlas dataset at 500 m resolution. The full file is large and download-gated by a user-information form, so Kerala 2040 does not silently mirror it.

ksdma.note: KSDMA publishes flood probability rasters and GSI landslide-susceptibility shapefiles suitable for explicit exclusion and stress-test layers.

bhuvan.note: Large GIS layers are catalogued separately from the lightweight web bundle.

kerala_forest.note: Used as an ecological exclusion source alongside national protected-area datasets.

kspcb.note: Supports circular-industry mass-flow and disposal-baseline work.

ppac.note: Used for non-electric energy context and transport-fuel trajectories.

vahan.organisation: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways / VAHAN
vahan.note: Kerala Economic Review is used as the reproducible fallback for current EV counts.

kmml.note: Candidate primary circular-industry case; quantitative claims require a mass balance.

fact.note: Candidate industrial-symbiosis source for post-baseline expansion.

bess_4h.note: The CEA table reports the 4-hour BESS cost trajectory as a range. This registry preserves the published values without silently assigning unverified year labels to each endpoint.

model_input_grid.rule: Null values are intentional. Final optimisation must fail input validation if a required techno-economic field is unresolved. External study benchmarks above are not defaults.

scenario_dimensions.rule: This file defines which levers differ between scenarios. Numerical values enter only after a source or explicit scenario assumption is recorded in a dedicated input dataset.
